description:
The reader's daily brief, or a public edition's morning: the briefing's lines by section, each with its
countries, who it is about, its score (the story's main at its section's place, the world in a World section, else the edition's home, 0-1) and `mains` (the main at home and at the world), our story page
and the outlet; its `pulse` (the loud stories the briefing did not tell, by column, each line with its outlets
and the first one's link); its `events` (worth going to: when, where, its link), and what was read for it. The
recording reads the same. With no `edition`, the reader's daily brief (made each day from their
interests; its `own` note says whether it is ready), else the World edition; edition='my' asks it too.
`edition` world, pl or us names a public edition; `date` YYYY-MM-DD (the latest when omitted), with no edition
the reader's own of that day, or the edition it would have been built on when none was made (`own` says);
`audio` adds that edition read aloud: `audio.label` names whose recording it is (a reader with none of their own
hears the edition theirs is built on), `audio.says` why there is none. Its words are in `language`: the
edition's own (the Polish edition in Polish) unless asked or the reader chose another.

edition.description: world, pl or us, a public edition. Omitted or my (or own): the reader's own, with `date` theirs of that day.

language.description: ISO 639-1, such as en or pl: the words in that language where the edition offers it; omitted, the language the reader reads it in (the Polish edition's is Polish). The answer's `language` says which.

name: morning
title: Morning edition
